name: Reticular Perineurioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Reticular Perineurioma

criteria.description: Presence of reticular (net-like) proliferation of spindle-shaped perineurial cells with characteristic whorled and storiform patterns
Positive immunostaining for epithelial membrane antigen (EMA) and claudin-1 with negative S-100 protein staining
Solitary, slow-growing, painless subcutaneous or dermal nodule typically located on extremities or trunk

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of reticular perineurial cell proliferation with positive EMA and claudin-1 immunostaining and negative S-100 protein staining
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other peripheral nerve sheath tumors such as schwannoma and neurofibroma.

laboratory: Immunohistochemical positivity for epithelial membrane antigen (EMA)
imaging: Ultrasound showing well-defined hypoechoic subcutaneous mass
MRI demonstrating a localized lesion with low to intermediate signal intensity on T1 and high signal on T2-weighted images without infiltration
genetic: No known recurrent genetic mutations identified
other: Histopathological examination revealing reticular pattern of perineurial cell proliferation
Electron microscopy showing characteristic perineurial cell features such as pinocytotic vesicles and basal lamina

distinguishingFeatures: Antoni A and B histological patterns
Absence of reticular perineurial cell proliferation
Mixed cellular composition including Schwann cells and fibroblasts
Lack of whorled reticular pattern typical of perineurioma
